about: Amateur prefix allocations by country/entity with approximate first/last use years, plus licence classes (Foundation/Intermediate/Full and national equivalents) where curated. Based on ITU Article 19 blocks, national licensing history, and DXCC entity changes. Not a legal document — verify critical details with national regulators.

entries.summary: Ofcom issues Foundation, Intermediate, and Full (Advanced) licences. Callsign structure depends on level and home nation (England, Scotland, Wales, NI, Crown Dependencies).

periods.prefixes: G, M, 2E/2M/2W/2I, M3/M6/M7, GM, GW, GI, GD, GJ, GU, MM, MW, MI, MD, MJ, MG
periods.note: ITU block G*; regional second letter/digit in legacy G calls — see Callsign series below.

licences.callsigns: M3xxx, M6xxx, M7xxx (England); MM6/M7 (Scotland); MW6/M7 (Wales); MI6/M7 (NI); similar on GD/GJ/GU
licences.privileges: 10 W PEP (most bands); Foundation band plan — limited HF (e.g. 80/40/20/15/10 m segments), VHF/UHF.
licences.note: M7 is the current Foundation issue block (replacing M6 for new licences).

licences.privileges: 50 W PEP; wider HF than Foundation but not all Full bands; cannot operate on all Advanced-only segments.
licences.note: Leading 2 marks Intermediate; nation letter E/M/W/I as per Full.

licences.callsigns: M0, MM0, MW0, MI0, MD0, MJ0, MG0 + suffix; legacy G… calls remain valid
licences.privileges: Up to 400 W PEP on UK amateur bands; all allocations in the UK amateur licence schedule.
licences.note: New Full issues use M+0; Scotland/Wales/NI use MM0, MW0, MI0, etc.

licences.callsigns: G + digit + suffix (e.g. G3VZL, G4EA5) — retained for life
licences.privileges: Treated as Full; original Class A/B distinctions abolished but callsigns kept.
licences.note: Second digit G1–G8 indicated regional issue block (see series table), not Foundation/Intermediate.

licences.callsigns: 2-letter regional prefixes (e.g. G3… with restricted privileges in early decades)
licences.privileges: Historically restricted HF; merged into modern licence framework by 2003 reform.
licences.note: Superseded by Foundation / Intermediate / Full structure.

entries.summary: FCC three-class system: Technician, General, Extra. Exam Element credits (formerly written tests). Vanity calls follow group rules by class.

licences.callsigns: Group C/D: district K/W/N + 3 letters (e.g. K1ABC); any unassigned block
licences.privileges: All privileges above 30 MHz; HF on specified segments (expanded over time — Tech HF bands).
licences.note: Entry-level; Element 2 + Element 3 (or credit) for General/Extra path.

licences.callsigns: Same pool as Technician; historically distinguished by exam, not prefix
licences.privileges: Most HF amateur bands; not all Extra-only segments (e.g. some 80/75/20/15 edges).

licences.callsigns: Group A/B preferred: 1×2, 2×1, 1×3 (e.g. K1A, AA1A, W1AW); shorter = older Extra
licences.privileges: All US amateur bands and modes; maximum spectrum access.

licences.callsigns: K/W/N + 2×3 with N or W as second letter in some eras
licences.privileges: Limited HF/VHF; CW/digital segments; no longer issued.
Between General and Extra; merged into Extra class 2012.
HF/VHF per Basic qualification; some bands need Honours.
Full HF amateur spectrum in Canada.
